title: Quickstart Templates Launch Retro (Week 1)
summary: Internal retro on the Quickstart Templates launch week (RAG, Agents, RAG+Agents) and docs-site integration. Team reviewed what worked (activation, repo scaffolding, observability pack, SDK helper changes) and what didn’t (429/backoff confusion, streaming behind proxies, CI flakes, dashboards import friction, env var naming drift). Agreed on a short patch release + a maintenance rhythm (monthly dependency bumps, ownership rotation, release checklist).
topics: Top support ticket drivers (429s, streaming disconnects, timeouts on large docs)
Telemetry contract v1: cardinality and required fields
CI smoke test flakiness and staging instability
Next iteration: backends, Go, eval harness hooks
questions: Do we want templates to default to retrying 429s, or should the sample code be more explicit about customer quotas?
Should request_id be required for template apps to start, or best-effort with warnings?
Are we comfortable calling the dashboards bundle “default” if some panels are empty until users enable token attribution?
Do we need a dedicated “proxy / load balancer” section for streaming in every template README?
next_steps: Ship quick patch release (v1.0.1) across repos: clearer 429 guidance, proxy streaming notes, and env var consistency lint fixes.
Update docs-site pages to add “Known issues” callouts and link to workarounds (timeouts on ingest, streaming behind proxy).
Reduce CI flakes: pin staging model route for smoke tests and add retries for the telemetry assertion step.
Add “Observability pack import” walkthrough video/gif and a copy-pastable curl check for telemetry fields.
Stand up a monthly template maintenance cadence (dependency updates + smoke tests + docs drift scan).
action_items: Talia Benson — create maintenance rotation doc + monthly release calendar; include on-call style owner for launch week; due 2026-02-16
Dev Patel — compile top 10 launch-week questions (Slack + Jira + Intercom) and map each to a doc/README fix; due 2026-02-17
Monica Patel — update Python SDK helper docs snippet: explicit 429 backoff example + idempotency note; due 2026-02-18
Dana Lo — add proxy/ingress streaming troubleshooting section to TypeScript template + docs links; due 2026-02-18
Sahana Iyer — investigate CI smoke test flake (telemetry assertion timing) and add bounded retries + better logs; due 2026-02-19
Sergio Costa — improve observability pack import README: required env vars, expected panels, and “empty dashboard” troubleshooting; due 2026-02-19
Logan Wright — confirm telemetry contract v1 guidance on cardinality for tenant/user fields and update the contract doc with examples; due 2026-02-20
Naomi Feldman — review new “PII and logging” wording for templates + ensure pre-commit secret scanning instructions are consistent; due 2026-02-20
Elliot Price — add a short “Production checklist” section to docs landing page highlighting timeouts/retries/429s and link to known issues; due 2026-02-20

transcript:
Quickstart Templates Launch Retro (Week 1)
Recorded by Fireflies
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 9:05 AM PT
Duration: 52 minutes

Attendees:
- Talia Benson (PM, DevEx)
- Alex Martinez (DX sponsor)
- Monica Patel (SDK)
- Ibrahim Khan (SDK TL)
- Dana Lo (TypeScript template lead)
- Sabrina James (SDK examples)
- Elliot Price (Docs)
- Wei Chen (Docs owner)
- Renee Sullivan (Advocacy)
- Logan Wright (Telemetry)
- Allison Grant (Observability standards)
- Sergio Costa (Dashboards/alerts)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Naomi Feldman (Security)
- Connor O'Brien (Release/process)
- Sahana Iyer (CI/build)
- Dev Patel (Support insights)
- Owen Phillips (Supportability)
- Dylan Brooks (Console liaison)

---

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright. Let’s get started. This is the retro for launch week of quickstart templates. Goal today is: what went well, what didn’t, and then concrete follow-ups. Not a blame thing.

[00:18] Alex Martinez: Yep, and I’d like us to leave with two things: one patch release scope, and then a maintenance rhythm so we don’t end up with like, three-month-old quickstarts.

[00:30] Elliot Price: And also, doc drift. Please. I got like five pings that code blocks don’t match master, which is… not true, but it’s close enough that it looks true.

[00:42] (crosstalk)

[00:44] Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll do quick framing. We shipped: Python RAG template, TypeScript RAG template, Agents template, combined RAG+agent template. Observability pack. Docs landing pages. CI smoke tests. And the SDK helper updates.

[01:03] Dev Patel: And Support got… not slammed, but like a first wave. Mostly 429 confusion, and streaming disconnect stuff.

[01:11] Talia Benson: Yup, we’ll cover. First: wins. Alex, you want to kick off?

[01:18] Alex Martinez: Win number one, we hit the “15 minutes to first run” for internal dogfood pretty consistently. Like, even people who weren’t on the project got it working. That’s huge.

[01:30] Renee Sullivan: I’ll add: the reference app demo worked in the launch brief. Like, actually worked. No demo gods needed.

[01:37] Dylan Brooks: Console side, I saw good usage of the trace deep links. People clicked from template logs to Console traces. That was the point.

[01:46] Logan Wright: Telemetry-wise: the templates are emitting the right shape most of the time. I saw request_id, model, route, tenant. Some folks are missing tenant, but we didn’t want to hard-fail them.

[01:58] Allison Grant: Also the cardinality guardrails in the docs were good. Like, we didn’t say “log user_email” as a label anywhere. Small miracles.

[02:06] Sean Gallagher: SRE perspective: timeouts and retries were at least present. We’ve seen so many examples in the wild that do infinite retries. We didn’t.

[02:16] Monica Patel: The SDK helper got traction. Like, people copy pasted the streaming wrapper. That’s why we did it.

[02:23] Talia Benson: Great. Okay, what didn’t go well. Dev, you already hinted.

[02:29] Dev Patel: Yeah. Biggest confusion: 429. People read “we retry” and assume it’ll just work. But if your quota is too low, it will never work. So we need wording like “retries help with burst limits, not sustained over-quota.”

[02:47] Owen Phillips: Also supportability: the error messages in one template say “rate limit hit” but don’t include like “check REDWOOD_RATE_LIMIT_BUDGET” or whatever. They just say “try again.”

[02:56] Dana Lo: On TypeScript template, I think we didn’t surface the retry config in the README enough. It exists in code, but it’s not in the “first 5 minutes” path.

[03:08] Ibrahim Khan: Slight correction: the retry behavior differs between streaming and non-streaming. And that’s where confusion comes in. The “stream reconnect” story isn’t the same as “retry the whole request.” We tried to keep it safe, but docs are not crisp.

[03:25] Talia Benson: Okay, streaming disconnects. Dana, can you talk about what we’re seeing?

[03:30] Dana Lo: Yeah. Customers behind proxies or like corporate ingress see the connection close around 60 seconds or so. And then they think Redwood is dropping it. Sometimes it’s their proxy buffer. We need a section: “If you’re behind Nginx/Cloudflare/ALB, set these timeouts, disable buffering,” etc.

[03:52] Sean Gallagher: Yeah, and also just: SSE over some proxies is pain. Even if Redwood is fine.

[03:58] Rafael Mendes: The templates should emit a log line when streaming ends unexpectedly, with a hint. Not “Unhandled error: socket hang up.”

[04:07] Monica Patel: The SDK PR we did improved it, but not a silver bullet. We should show “client reconnect” pattern and mention “idempotency key” if you retry.

[04:20] Talia Benson: Noted. Next issue: timeouts on large docs ingestion.

[04:26] Dev Patel: We have a Jira from a customer already. The ingest worker defaults were okay for small doc sets, but for like “company handbook pdfs” it just times out. It’s the chunking + embedding batching. Needs a “big docs” config.

[04:43] Sabrina James: That’s kind of expected; we set conservative defaults. But we didn’t make the knob obvious. Like, “increase INGEST_CONCURRENCY, increase EMBED_BATCH_SIZE” or whatever.

[04:53] Logan Wright: Also, if they crank concurrency, telemetry gets noisier. But that’s okay. We can document “if you do this, watch your 429s on embeddings.”

[05:04] Sergio Costa: And our dashboard pack has a 429 panel, but it isn’t prominent. Maybe we make “rate limits” row above the fold.

[05:14] Talia Benson: Cool. Now docs-site issues. Elliot, you mentioned drift.

[05:19] Elliot Price: Drift plus snippet extraction failures. We had that deploy job fail once, because a README changed format and our extractor couldn’t find the fence. It’s brittle.

[05:33] Wei Chen: Also the docs talk about env vars that changed names in the last PR. Like we say REDWOOD_API_KEY in one place and REDWOOD_KEY in another. I think we fixed most of it but not all.

[05:46] Connor O'Brien: That’s part of release automation too. If we can’t reliably extract “the canonical snippet,” docs will always lag.

[05:56] Sahana Iyer: The snippet extractor fails are annoying but fixable. We need conventions in READMEs. Like “BEGIN_SNIPPET: quickstart-install” markers. Then it’s deterministic.

[06:10] Talia Benson: Great. Let’s capture: add snippet markers and a lint.

[06:16] Naomi Feldman: On the security side, I want to call out a win and a miss. Win: no one is telling people to paste keys into code. Miss: the .env guidance is a bit too casual. It says “copy .env.example to .env” but doesn’t say “never commit it” until later.

[06:33] Owen Phillips: +1. People stop reading after “copy this.”

[06:36] Naomi Feldman: And the logging section says “redact PII” but doesn’t give a concrete example of what we consider PII in prompts. Like, names, emails, MRNs in healthcare, etc.

[06:48] Renee Sullivan: For advocacy, we’re getting asked in community: “does Redwood store my prompts?” We need consistent language. The templates currently mention retention but not in the first page.

[07:00] Dylan Brooks: Product-wise, we have the official stance in docs. We can link rather than re-explain. But we should link.

[07:07] Talia Benson: Okay. Now observability pack feedback. Sergio?

[07:12] Sergio Costa: People like the dashboards but importing is confusing. They don’t know where to paste JSON. Console has a flow, but it’s not obvious. And if token attribution isn’t enabled, some panels are blank, which makes them think it’s broken.

[07:29] Allison Grant: We should label panels “requires token attribution” or similar. Otherwise it looks like we’re missing data.

[07:36] Logan Wright: Also, the telemetry contract says metric names, but not “expected lag.” There’s ingestion delay. Some folks refresh and expect immediate data.

[07:45] Sean Gallagher: Alert hygiene: I’m glad we didn’t ship paging alerts by default. But we should explain burn-rate style and that these are examples, not a promise.

[07:57] Talia Benson: Good. CI and smoke tests. Sahana?

[08:02] Sahana Iyer: We had flakes in the telemetry assertion step. Like, the app sends traces but the check runs before they land in the backend. So it fails randomly.

[08:14] Ibrahim Khan: So we need to either poll with backoff, or assert locally that spans were created before shipping.

[08:22] Sahana Iyer: We already do local OTel exporter in CI, but the “Console visible” check is the flaky one. We can add bounded retries, and also pin the staging route so we don’t hit model rollouts mid-test.

[08:38] Dylan Brooks: Yeah we had a small canary that moved latency around, which shouldn’t break tests but it did because timeouts are tight.

[08:47] Sean Gallagher: Timeouts in CI should be longer than production defaults. Counterintuitive, but tests need stability.

[08:56] Talia Benson: Okay. Now, let’s do the retro exercise: keep / stop / start. I’ll go around quickly.

[09:04] Alex Martinez: Keep: one contract across languages. Stop: shipping anything without a “known issues” section. Start: monthly patch release cadence.

[09:16] Monica Patel: Keep: SDK helper as the canonical way. Stop: template code diverging from SDK docs. Start: in-repo “recipes” folder for 429, streaming behind proxy, big docs.

[09:31] Dana Lo: Keep: env var schema. Stop: different env var names in TS vs Python. Start: pre-commit that fails if README mentions a var not in the config schema.

[09:46] Elliot Price: Keep: docs pages that are template-first, not product brochure. Stop: manual snippet copy. Start: snippet markers + automated extraction.

[10:00] Logan Wright: Keep: telemetry contract v1. Stop: people adding high-cardinality labels in examples. Start: add explicit examples of “allowed tenant_id formats” and what not to do.

[10:15] Sergio Costa: Keep: dashboards bundle. Stop: assuming people know how to import. Start: short walkthrough + “what good looks like” screenshots.

[10:27] Naomi Feldman: Keep: safe defaults around secrets. Stop: burying “don’t commit .env” in paragraph 8. Start: a security callout box at the top.

[10:40] Sean Gallagher: Keep: timeouts set by default. Stop: “retry everything” vibes. Start: guidance on when to fail fast and surface to user.

[10:51] Dev Patel: Keep: error taxonomy. Stop: vague errors. Start: map each common support question to a single URL we can paste.

[11:04] Talia Benson: Great. Let’s talk patch release scope. Connor, what’s realistic?

[11:10] Connor O'Brien: We can do v1.0.1 within a week if it’s mostly docs + small code changes. If we change behavior, it’s riskier.

[11:18] Monica Patel: For SDK helper, we can add examples and maybe tweak default backoff messaging without changing actual retry policy.

[11:27] Dana Lo: For TS template, I can add the proxy section and improve error messages without changing core logic.

[11:36] Sahana Iyer: CI fixes can go in parallel.

[11:40] Talia Benson: Okay so v1.0.1: (1) 429 docs and sample backoff, (2) streaming behind proxy section + log hint, (3) big docs ingestion knobs doc, (4) env var naming consistency lint, (5) observability pack import docs improvements, (6) CI flake reduction.

[12:03] Alex Martinez: And please add “Known issues” to every template README. Even if it’s short.

[12:10] Wei Chen: We already have a known issues page in Confluence, but it’s not linked. We can link it and also keep a copy in repo.

[12:18] Elliot Price: Better in repo. People don’t have Confluence access externally.

[12:23] Talia Benson: Good point.

[12:26] Dylan Brooks: Also product messaging: we should be careful not to promise “Dedicated/Private readiness” beyond what we have. The templates show a path, but not a fully supported helm chart.

[12:39] Rafael Mendes: Yeah, but at least the k8s manifests exist. We should label them “minimal.”

[12:44] (crosstalk)

[12:46] Talia Benson: Okay. Metrics. Alex asked for activation. Renee, anything from community?

[12:53] Renee Sullivan: Mostly positive. People liked that we show OpenTelemetry from day one. But a bunch of folks asked “do I need Jaeger?” Like, they don’t want to run observability stack locally.

[13:07] Logan Wright: We should say “it works without it, but if you run the compose stack, you get traces.” Also the Console deep link works regardless once deployed.

[13:17] Sergio Costa: The compose stack includes the vector DB, but not always the OTel collector. We made it optional and maybe that’s confusing.

[13:26] Ibrahim Khan: Optional is good, but defaults must be clear. Like one command that works.

[13:33] Talia Benson: Okay. “one command path” stays. Optional extras are spelled out.

[13:40] Naomi Feldman: One more security thing: tool calling allow-list defaults. In the agent template we did allow-list, but the docs still say “add any tools you want.” That sentence needs to be reworded.

[13:53] Sabrina James: I can fix that. It should say “explicitly register allowed tools” and add a warning.

[13:58] Talia Benson: Great.

[14:01] Allison Grant: On telemetry contract: we should add a section about “tenant_id: stable pseudonymous ID, not email.” I keep seeing folks in Slack ask if they should put org name.

[14:14] Owen Phillips: Support asks for “tenant_id” to debug, but yeah, it can be like hashed org id.

[14:22] Talia Benson: Okay, we’ll update.

[14:25] Sean Gallagher: Can we talk about alert thresholds? Our example has p95 latency alert at like 2 seconds and that’s not universal.

[14:34] Sergio Costa: We tried to use burn-rate style, but yeah, the copy says “recommended.” We should say “starting point.”

[14:43] Rafael Mendes: And tell people to tune per model and per region.

[14:47] Dylan Brooks: We can reference Console rollouts and fallback policies too, like “if 5xx rises, route to fallback.” But that’s advanced.

[14:58] Talia Benson: We’ll keep it in “Next steps / advanced ops” section.

[15:02] (pause)

[15:04] Talia Benson: Alright, we’re at minute 15. Let’s jump to “what do we do differently next iteration.” Like, v1.1 ideas.

[15:11] Alex Martinez: Two things: more backends and more evaluation guidance. People ask “which vector DB?” We picked one default, but we need the adapter story clearer.

[15:22] Ibrahim Khan: And eval harness. We have a minimal prompt set but templates don’t show “how to run eval after you change prompts.” That’s a miss.

[15:32] Renee Sullivan: For agents, I want a “tool safety checklist” page. Like, not a research paper, just practical.

[15:39] Naomi Feldman: Yes. Especially around network tools. If you allow a “fetch_url” tool, you have SSRF risk. We should say it.

[15:49] Dana Lo: For TypeScript, we got requests for Next.js variant. Right now it’s Express-ish. We can consider Next API routes.

[16:00] Talia Benson: Noted. But focus: stabilize v1 first.

[16:04] Connor O'Brien: Also versioning policy. We shipped tags but we need a compatibility matrix with SDK versions. People pin versions.

[16:13] Elliot Price: And docs should mention “use template tag v1.0.x.” Not “clone main.”

[16:19] Monica Patel: Yeah, because SDK versions move.

[16:23] Talia Benson: Great. Now I’m going to read back action items, we’ll assign owners. (Fireflies will capture but let’s be explicit.)

[16:33] Talia Benson: 1) Maintenance rotation + calendar. I’ll take.

[16:37] Talia Benson: 2) Support roundup top questions and single URL answers. Dev, can you own?

[16:42] Dev Patel: Yes.

[16:43] Talia Benson: 3) SDK helper doc snippet updates: Monica.

[16:47] Monica Patel: Yep.

[16:48] Talia Benson: 4) TS template proxy streaming troubleshooting: Dana.

[16:52] Dana Lo: Yes.

[16:53] Talia Benson: 5) CI flakes: Sahana.

[16:56] Sahana Iyer: Yep.

[16:58] Talia Benson: 6) Observability pack import README improvements: Sergio.

[17:02] Sergio Costa: Got it.

[17:04] Talia Benson: 7) Telemetry contract cardinality examples update: Logan.

[17:08] Logan Wright: Yep.

[17:10] Talia Benson: 8) Security wording review on .env / PII / allow-list language: Naomi.

[17:14] Naomi Feldman: Yes.

[17:16] Talia Benson: 9) Docs landing page “production checklist” plus known issues callout: Elliot.

[17:20] Elliot Price: Yep.

[17:21] Talia Benson: 10) v1.0.1 release checklist and tagging alignment: Connor.

[17:26] Connor O'Brien: Yep.

[17:28] Talia Benson: Great.

[17:30] Alex Martinez: One more: do we want a short internal “launch week playbook” for next time? Like, who watches dashboards, who answers Slack.

[17:38] Talia Benson: Good call, I’ll add under maintenance plan.

[17:42] (crosstalk)

[17:44] Rafael Mendes: Also, can we fix the template logs to include correlation IDs consistently? I saw one service logging requestId and another logging req_id.

[17:52] Allison Grant: That should be in the lint. Telemetry contract says request_id.

[17:58] Ibrahim Khan: That’s a code fix in Python template too, I think.

[18:03] Talia Benson: Okay, put that in v1.0.1 if it’s small.

[18:07] Dylan Brooks: And confirm the API echoes request_id header consistently. We did that PR, but not sure if everyone’s using it.

[18:14] Monica Patel: The SDK propagates traceparent, but request_id echo is separate. We can mention it.

[18:20] Talia Benson: Cool.

[18:23] Sean Gallagher: Last thing from SRE: please, please, make it clear that “retry on 500” has a cap. And that you should have a circuit breaker upstream if you’re calling LLMs in user-facing paths.

[18:35] Dana Lo: We have max attempts, but yeah it’s not front and center.

[18:38] Talia Benson: Got it.

[18:41] Elliot Price: We can add a “Failure modes” section. Like, what errors mean and what to do.

[18:48] Owen Phillips: Yes. That’s exactly what support needs.

[18:51] Talia Benson: Okay.

[18:53] Talia Benson: We’re good. Any blockers to v1.0.1 next week?

[18:58] Sahana Iyer: Only if staging keeps flapping, but we can isolate tests.

[19:02] Connor O'Brien: If changes are mostly docs, it’s fine.

[19:05] Naomi Feldman: I just need to review the updated security wording, but it’s not huge.

[19:09] Talia Benson: Okay. Recap: overall successful launch, first wave issues are normal, we’ll address with patch + docs + maintenance cadence.

[19:17] Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone. This was good. Let’s not lose momentum.

[19:20] Talia Benson: Meeting adjourned.
